html:
The U'wa are a Chibchan speaking people of the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy in northeastern Colombia, in the cloud forests and valleys between the Andes and the eastern plains.

They farm, hunt and fish, and their beliefs treat the land and what lies beneath it as sacred. Their neighbours in the 1400s included the Muisca and the Guane to the west. Spanish conquest and missions pushed them up into the mountains. In the 1990s the U'wa became known worldwide for their fight against oil drilling by Occidental Petroleum on their land: they said oil was the blood of the earth and threatened collective suicide if drilling went ahead. The company left the area in the early 2000s.
sum: The U'wa are a Chibchan speaking people of the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy in northeastern Colombia, in the cloud forests and valleys between the Andes and the eastern plains.
